limitations: A statewide map of plant communities made from plots, imagery and models: each polygon is a best estimate for that patch, not a survey of your site.
Polygons are generalised by the service (about 20 m) before they reach the app, so small patches such as a wet gully or a rock outcrop can be lost.
Each cell takes the most common vegetation class of 9 sample points; a wet-gully strip narrower than a cell is only flagged, not mapped.
It shows what grows there, not how much fuel there is now: fuel load also depends on the time since the last fire (fire history).

items.formula: measured: every typed array of the scenario, 6.6 MB
items.label: Scenario data (terrain, fuel, 10 m ground, fire history, places)

items.formula: the same bytes again: the scenario is copied (not moved) to the worker so the screen keeps its own
items.label: The simulation worker's copy of the scenario

items.formula: 40,000 cells x 548.4 B + 57.0 KB front bookkeeping
items.label: Fire spread state
items.note: Grows a little with the burning front.

items.formula: 40,000 cells x 105.4 B + 2,025 columns x 60 B
items.label: Insight engine (why the fire does what it does)

items.formula: measured: 2 copies of the 3.5 MB fuel map (the base and the edited one)
items.label: Working copies of the fuel map (edits apply to them)
Wind, sun and environment rasters on the fire grid

items.formula: 2,025 columns x 20 levels of 133 m: 11.9 KB per column + 40,000 cells x 260.5 B
items.label: Atmosphere model (3-D, 20 terrain-following levels)

items.formula: 4,000 embers x 107 B + 40,000 cells x 37 B
items.label: Ember particles and landing maps
items.note: Grows with the burning front (its lists of burning cells).

items.formula: 7 x about 5.7 MB (40,000 cells x 95.1 B + 2,025 columns x 918.6 B), ring capped at 80.0 MB
items.label: Checkpoints for rewind (7: the start and every 30 min)
items.note: Checkpoints taken while a large fire burns are bigger.

items.formula: 37 keyframes x 1.6 MB + 181 frames x 9.0 KB + fire arrays; kept under 157.3 MB (older history is thinned)
items.label: Time-scrubber history (fire front, keyframes every 5 min, one frame per step)

items.formula: 320 x 320 samples: positions 12 B + triangle indices + a 4 B shade texel each (estimate)
items.label: Ground mesh and shading texture

items.formula: 40,000 cells x about 16 B (about four float textures; estimate)
items.label: Fire and heat-map textures on the fire grid

items.formula: up to 32,000 tree instances x about 80 B (estimate)
items.label: Trees drawn in 3-D

notes: Auto tier: shown for Standard, where every run starts; the app may switch to Fast after timing this device, which uses less.
The scenario data and the fuel copies are measured; the rest of the engine, the scrubber history and the GPU are modelled from the grid sizes.
Engine figures reproduce measured runs within a few per cent (coefficients measured 2026-09-30 from the engine's own arrays).
GPU figures are estimates: WebGL does not report how much memory it uses.
JavaScript objects (feature lists, labels, closures) are not counted: typed arrays hold nearly all the data.
